Collapse factor-expanded t-statistic columns into group summaries

Source: R/collapseFactorTstats.R
collapseFactorTstats.Rd

When a factor variable (e.g. batch) or a multi-level character variable (e.g. population) is included in the regression model, the wide output of qtlRegressionStats() contains one t.<var><level> column per level. This function identifies groups of such columns by regular-expression patterns, replaces each group with the root-mean-square (RMS) of its t-statistics, and returns a leaner data frame suitable for PCA.

Usage

collapseFactorTstats(
  wide_df,
  patterns = list(batch = "^t\\.factor_batch_", population = "^t\\.population")
)

Arguments

wide_df

A wide data frame from qtlRegressionStats() with t_only = TRUE.

patterns

A named list of regular expressions. Each element matches a set of columns to collapse; the name becomes the new column name (prefixed with "t."). Defaults to patterns that detect the MAGE chr17 dataset's batch and population indicator columns.

Value

wide_df with matched column groups replaced by single t.<name> RMS columns.

Examples

exdir <- system.file("extdata", package = "tQTLExperiment")
tqe   <- tQTLExperiment(
    plinkPrefix = file.path(exdir, "chr22-n100"),
    phenoFile   = file.path(exdir, "mean-pheno-n100.bed"),
    covFile     = file.path(exdir, "cov-n100-tqtl.tsv"),
    genome      = "hg38"
)
#> Extracting number of samples and rownames from chr22-n100.fam...
#> Extracting number of variants and colnames from chr22-n100.bim...
tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)
res <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1")
collapsed <- collapseFactorTstats(res)
